**HR Business Partner - International Role

**Experienced HR professional with an international mindset?

We are looking for an experienced and trusted HR Business Partner who enjoys working close to managers, employees and colleagues at our headquarters in Pårup.

This is an international role in which you will support selected business areas across countries and cultures throughout the employee journey. You will advise managers on organisational development, employee relations, recruitment, employment conditions and day-to-day leadership matters. You will also be responsible for coordinating and developing MASCOT's trainee programmes.

You will join an experienced HR team and report to the HR Manager.

Your key responsibilities

• Advise and support managers on leadership, employee relations and organisational development

• Manage recruitment processes from job profile to final employment

• Handle employee cases, including absence, difficult conversations, terminations and exit interviews

• Ensure compliance with employment legislation, contracts, policies and local employment conditions

• Plan and quality-assure onboarding activities

• Support international HR projects, employee surveys, workshops and annual HR activities

• Coordinate trainee recruitment, training plans and ongoing development

• Collaborate with managers and colleagues across MASCOT's international organisation

What you bring

You have at least five years of experience as an HR Business Partner or HR Consultant. You are confident in advising managers and comfortable handling both operational HR matters and broader organisational topics in an international business environment.

You are structured, responsible and able to move tasks from initiation to completion. You communicate clearly, listen carefully and build trusted relationships across functions, countries and cultures. You use your business understanding to combine sound judgement with a practical and solution-oriented approach.

Experience with recruitment, employment law, coaching, conflict management and HR systems is important. Knowledge of SAP SuccessFactors and LinkedIn Recruiter is an advantage.

You are fluent in written and spoken English. Fluency in another European language would be a strong advantage.

What we offer

At MASCOT, you become part of a family-owned international company with strong values, ambitious goals and short decision-making paths.

• An international HR role based at our headquarters in Pårup

• A permanent onsite position with close collaboration across the organisation

• A professional and supportive HR team

• Pension, health insurance and wellbeing initiatives

• Excellent food in our staff restaurant

• Employee discounts on MASCOT workwear

Ready to make a difference?

Apply today. We review applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis.

At MASCOT, we are united by passion, collaboration and the ambition to develop, manufacture and deliver the world's best workwear and safety footwear.

jobs.occupation: Driver at Arla Foods Garage - Ishøj/Copenhagen
jobs.description:
Would you like to work at Arla Foods Garage in Ishøj as a driver ?

Arla Foods is an exciting dairy company that operates 24/7. We deliver the day´s milk to grocery stores in the Copenhagen area and North Zealand at the agreed time.

Our wish for a new colleague would be

• You greatly appreciate collaboration and you are happy to lend a hand where needed.

• You are flexible, able to meet deadlines, and good at keeping an overview when things are going fast.

• You have agreed that we will start early, i.e. you must also be able to meet at 0245.

• You are prepared to work at least every other weekend.

• It is an advantage if you have experience with distribution driving, preferably with refrigerated goods.

• It is expected that you can speak and understand Danish or English.

• That you have at least a CE driving license.

• EU continuing education and a driving license are necessity.

• We comply with all regulations and you should expect a working week of 37 hours.

• We also operate on a number of public holidays, so you should be prepared to be called to work on such days.

Application and contact

If the above sounds like something to you, you are welcome to send an application, where you are also asked to attach your CV, briefly describing your professional experience.

Once you have submitted your application, you will receive a receipt, and only if we subsequently have a job that fits your personal profile will we contact you.

You can call Team leads Carsten F. Rasmussen or Steen H. Jensen on phone 91 31 48 48, between 0700 and 1300 on weekdays, if you would like information about the job.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Do you enjoy finding the biggest commercial opportunities, improving customer journeys, and turning data into initiatives that drive measurable growth? Keep reading!

At Limepack, E-commerce is at the heart of how we acquire and convert customers across Europe. As we grow, we see significant potential to improve the customer journey and webshop performance across our markets, while becoming much better at what happens after the first purchase: building stronger relationships, increasing repeat purchases, and growing customer lifetime value.

With our current E-commerce Manager going on maternity leave, this role has a unique starting point. You’ll initially take ownership of E-commerce growth and customer journey optimisation, but this is not simply a 10–12 month maternity cover. The role is designed to evolve with you: over time, your focus will shift towards becoming Limepack’s Loyalty Lead, taking long-term ownership of Post-Purchase, CRM & Lifecycle.

This is a role for someone who combines commercial thinking with strong execution. You’ll use data to identify where the biggest opportunities are, set priorities, and drive initiatives across teams, taking responsibility for turning ideas into measurable results.

📋 Your responsibilities and impact

Your focus will evolve as you grow into the role: starting with E-commerce and gradually taking ownership of Loyalty, CRM, Email and Lifecycle.

• Grow E-commerce performance: Own and improve webshop conversion, customer journeys, AOV and revenue across markets. Identify the biggest opportunities and turn them into scalable improvements.

• Lead and collaborate across our tech setup: For the first 10–12 months, you will lead Alexander, our UX/Frontend Developer, who will report to you, while you report to our CCO. You will also work closely with our two Backend Developers and external partners to bring initiatives from idea to implementation.

• Turn data into priorities: Use customer and commercial data to understand where we should focus, build a clear roadmap, and follow up on the KPIs that matter.

• Drive projects from idea to impact: Lead high-impact initiatives across teams, create clear ownership, and make sure the right people and resources come together to deliver on time.

• Build for scale: Look beyond one-off improvements and create solutions that can work effectively across Limepack’s European markets.

• Build our Loyalty engine: After 10-12 months, own and improve the customer journey beyond the first purchase across Post-Purchase, CRM, Email and Lifecycle. Build stronger customer relationships, increase repeat purchases and grow customer lifetime value.

What success looks like: Within your first 12 months, you’ll aim to increase webshop conversion by 30%, help deliver our 2027 E-commerce revenue target of 40M in new business, and establish clear ownership and priorities for Loyalty. Longer term, you’ll drive improvements in repeat purchase rate, CLV and lifecycle revenue, including increasing first-to-second-purchase retention from 40% to 50%.

👉 Who you are

• You think commercially: You naturally look for the opportunities that will have the biggest impact on revenue and customer value, rather than simply working through a list of tasks.

• You are analytical and curious: You enjoy digging into data, understanding what customers are doing, and using those insights to decide what to improve next.

• You make things happen: You take ownership from opportunity to execution, create structure around projects, and follow through until the result is delivered.

• You are always looking for a better way: You enjoy improving customer journeys, processes and systems and think about how solutions can be scaled rather than solving the same problem repeatedly.

• You are strong across teams: You’re comfortable driving projects through people you don’t directly manage, aligning different stakeholders, and creating clarity around priorities and ownership.

🎓 Your experience

To succeed in this role, you should bring a strong combination of E-commerce experience, commercial thinking, analytical skills and project ownership.

• You have 3–5 years of relevant experience, ideally in E-commerce, digital growth, CRO, CRM, lifecycle marketing, or a similar commercially focused role.

• You have owned E-commerce performance and can point to measurable commercial results you personally helped create.

• You have hands-on experience with CRO and customer journey optimisation and know how to turn insights into improvements.

• You are strong with data, prioritization and project management, and are comfortable coordinating initiatives across multiple teams and stakeholders.

• Experience with CRM, lifecycle, retention or multi-market E-commerce is a strong advantage.

🚀 Who We Are

Limepack is a profitable Copenhagen-based European scale-up making custom-branded takeaway packaging accessible to businesses of all sizes. Since 2018, we’ve expanded across 14 countries by partnering with European manufacturers to offer faster, more affordable, and more sustainable packaging solutions.

We’re growing fast: we’ve been named a Børsen Gazelle four years in a row for exceptional revenue growth (Limepack.com/growth), and our ambition is to triple revenue over the next three years.

Today, we’re a team of 33 people, including 14 remote colleagues. We put a lot of emphasis on building a great place to work, and we’re proud to be a certified Happy Workplace (Limepack.com/happy). 🚀

💚 We offer:

• A full-time position based in Copenhagen with flexibility to work from home.

• A competitive salary based on experience.

• 6 weeks of paid time off, pay during sick days, and generous paid parental leave.

• The opportunity to take ownership of an important commercial area and grow from E-commerce ownership into leading Limepack’s Loyalty, CRM & Lifecycle agenda.

Principal Project Manager: Lead the future of PMO and SaaS delivery in media

Stibo DX is searching for an experienced Principal Project Manager to anchor our PMO and to drive the SaaS Delivery Model our project managers have built together; the standard for how we take the world's leading media groups from signed agreement to a live newsroom while running upgrade and migration projects of your own.

This is the role

In this newly defined role you anchor how Stibo DX delivers. Your job is to keep the Delivery Model moving, make the processes stick and make every project better than the last. The rest of your time goes to projects where you own scope, economics and the customer relationship. How the balance falls shifts with the portfolio, when a go-live needs you, the go-live wins.

You will join our Project Management team with employees located in Aarhus, Atlanta, Copenhagen, or Hamburg. You work side by side with our Principal Project Manager for Estimation & Standardization, who brings a deep knowledge of our product while you bring the method and the seniority.

More specifically, you will:

• Drive the SaaS Delivery Model with the team: take release 1.0 into use, aligned with internal stakeholders and keep the model and its artefact library current

• Anchor the PMO: the project model and standards, improve the rhythm-of-the-business, status reporting and the forecast and capacity inputs the executive team relies on

• Lead the feedback loop: retrospectives after every go-live, lessons written into estimation defaults and playbooks, and the numbers that show it works – estimate accuracy, margin and on-time go-lives

• Deliver upgrade and migration projects for existing customers – scope, economics and steering committees included

• Work with our workflow consultants to keep customers on the standard product: show how existing workflows solve the need before a change request is written, and decide with Product when a customization is worth it

What you bring

We are searching for a hands-on Principal who has built or run a delivery model or a PMO at a software vendor or implementation partner, knows that a model only works when the team owns it, understands how a services business makes money, and leads through credibility rather than hierarchy.

Moreover, you bring:

• 10+ years in IT or software project and programme management on the vendor side, including building or running a PMO or delivery model with a team that actually used it

• Commercial judgement: you have owned project budgets and change control, and you understand fixed price versus time and material, margin and billability

• Experience with SaaS onboarding or platform migrations, and comfort with technical scope such as integrations, data migration and cloud hosting

• An implementation background from ERP or CMS platforms is a plus: configuration before customization, and change management on the customer's side

• AI assistants already in your own project work – drafting, analysis, estimation – and a view on where they change the project manager's job

• Confidence in challenging the status quo while respecting what already works, a relevant certification (preferably PRINCE2), effortless English with Danish or German a plus, and willingness to travel around 10-20%

You do not have to tick every box – what matters is what you have delivered and how you did it.

How we work with AI

We run project management with AI in the loop – and we deliver AI into newsrooms. Administrative tasks have increasingly been automated using AI, as well as the projects themselves are supported by AI-enabled processes. On the customer side you will take Cue Autopilot – storyline automation, semantic tagging, image analysis – into live newsrooms. We expect you to use AI assistants as a matter of course in your own work, to be honest about where they fall short, and to help us take the next step.

Interested?

Please apply here on LinkedIn. You are encouraged to apply at your earliest convenience. Short-listed candidates will be invited for an interview. Applications are processed as they are received until the right candidate is found.

Should you have questions about the position, you are also welcome to contact Senior Vice President, Nikolaj Fisker via mail nifi@stibodx.com. We look forward to hearing from you.

Help us empower storytellers across the globe

Stibo DX is the global leader in digital transformation for media enterprises. Our platform and services help automate complex content production and enable omnichannel delivery for some of the world's most ambitious and successful media organizations.

We are a global and dynamic team of over 200 employees based in Aarhus, Copenhagen, Atlanta, Hamburg, Oslo, and Málaga, combining creativity and innovation with the stability of a long-standing organization.

Stibo DX is part of the Stibo Software Group, the second-largest Danish-owned software group. Our roots trace back to the Stibo Foundation, which has a 228-year history and a rich legacy that supports our continued growth.

Read the Stibo DX story and about working at Stibo DX.

Software Engineer, Technical Department, Cavendish Hydrogen, Herning

Are you ready to help advance the transition to clean mobility? At Cavendish Hydrogen, we are driven by a clear and vital mission: accelerating the global transition to zero-emission heavy-duty transportation. As a dedicated hydrogen fueling company, we design, deliver, and service cutting-edge hydrogen refueling stations (HRS) for customers across Europe, North America and Asia.

To support our growing international operations, we are looking for a curious, adaptable, and solution-oriented Software Engineer to join our Technical Department within Operations at our headquarters in Lind, Herning. In this role, you will contribute to the reliability, performance, and continuous improvement of our hydrogen refueling solutions, helping customers around the world transition to sustainable transportation.

About the job

As our Software Engineer you will connect our global field operations with our in-house software and innovation teams. You will be responsible for ensuring our customers’ hydrogen fueling stations perform safely, reliably, and efficiently across the globe. You will join an agile and collaborative Technical Department comprising of seven skilled colleagues. The team supports service technicians, project managers, and international customers.

Our software architecture is fully developed in-house. You will work closely with Application Engineering and the R&D Software Team to troubleshoot operational issues, implement software adjustments, and optimize live systems.

Key responsibilities and tasks

Operational support & advanced troubleshooting

• Provide software expertise to field service technicians, project teams, and global customers.

• Analyze machine telemetry, logs, and system data to identify operational issues.

• Conduct Root Cause Analyses (RCA) of software- and control-related incidents and coordinate corrective actions.

• Prioritize, manage, and escalate complex technical software challenges to relevant engineering teams.

Software adjustments & minor feature improvements

• Define, test, and deploy operational software adjustments, bug fixes, and site-specific parameter configurations.

• Implement urgent software updates while maintaining code integrity and alignment with the R&D Software Team.

• Translate field observations into clear specifications, user stories, and feature requests.

Remote commissioning support & knowledge sharing

• Support remote commissioning, factory testing, and system energization of new stations from our test facilities in Lind.

• Connect the Technical Department with Application Engineering and the R&D Software Team to support effective knowledge sharing and problem-solving.

About you

You may be a recent graduate ready to begin a career in green technology or an experienced engineer seeking meaningful industrial impact. Because our software is developed in-house, curiosity, structured problem-solving, and a willingness to learn are more important than experience with specific third-party tools.

Educational Background: You have a degree in Software Engineering, Automation & Control, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Relevant practical experience or an equivalent technical background is also welcome.

Interest in in-house software architecture: You are motivated to understand how software interacts with complex physical equipment including valves, compressors, cooling systems, and high-pressure gas controls.

PLC and automation experience: Experience with PLC programming in Structured Text under IEC 61131-3 is beneficial. Familiarity with Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 is an advantage but not a requirement.

Analytical approach: You are comfortable analyzing data and diagnostic logs and use a structured approach to root-cause investigation.

International flexibility: you can occasionally adjust your working hours to collaborate with colleagues and partners in North American or Asian time zones.

Language and communication: You communicate confidently in written and spoken English, our corporate language.

What we offer

Structured onboarding and mentoring: Experienced software and service engineers who will guide you through our software architecture and station design. Certified Beckhoff TwinCAT training may also be provided where relevant, and you will receive ongoing support from the R&D Software team.

Meaningful impact: Your work will help improve the uptime of commercial hydrogen refueling stations and keep zero-emission fleets operating.

Modern facilities in Lind: You will work in modern facilities with advanced test bays, a high-quality lunch canteen, an active staff association, and health insurance.

Flexibility & work-life balance: Your primary workplace and team will be based in Lind, with flexible working arrangements available.

No regular travel: You will support international remotely, without the need for frequent business travel.

Collaborative culture: You will join an informal and open workplace where questions, knowledge sharing, and autonomy are encouraged.

Apply now

Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

Curious to learn more?

For technical or role-specific questions, please contact Kim Hehlert, Technical Department Manager at +45 26 31 31 33.

For questions about the recruitment process, please contact Elsebeth Haarup Rasmussen, Head of HR, at +45 22 77 76 13.

Location: Lind, 7400 Herning, Denmark

IT Supporter

Would you also like to work in an international production environment where reliable IT is crucial to day-to-day operations? If so, you could be our new IT Support Specialist in Global IT, Gråsten.

At Global IT, you’ll have a varied workday where you’ll help colleagues with their IT challenges, work with modern Microsoft technologies, and support the IT infrastructure that keeps our production and business running. You’ll be part of a highly skilled team with both local and global connections.

IT plays a central role in our continued growth and development. As an IT Support Specialist, you’ll join a team of nine employees within a global IT organization comprising a total of 30 colleagues. Together, you’ll ensure stable, modern, and efficient IT solutions for the BHJ and Essentia Protein Solutions business units. You’ll have a broad role encompassing daily support, operations, troubleshooting, documentation, and the opportunity to contribute to projects and new solutions.

Primary tasks

Among other things, you will be working with:

• Level 1 and 2 IT support and help desk

• Support and administration of Microsoft 365 and Azure

• Support for business applications and IoT devices

• Installation, configuration, and maintenance of hardware and software

• Troubleshooting for clients, networks, and other IT infrastructure

• Administration of users, devices, and access rights

• Development of SOPs, user guides, and Knowledge Base articles

• Participation in IT projects and the implementation of new solutions

• Automation and optimization of processes

• Support for colleagues across our global locations

Personal profile

We envision that you have a solid IT skillset and thrive on both technical challenges and close contact with users.

You:

• Are a trained IT support specialist or have an equivalent IT background

• Have several years of experience providing IT support in a professional organization

• Have solid experience with Microsoft-based IT infrastructure

• Have experience with Microsoft Azure, Entra ID, and cloud-based solutions

• Have experience with Microsoft 365, including Exchange Online, Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint

• Have experience with networks, client management, and hardware

• Communicate professionally in both Danish and English, both verbally and in writing

• Work in a structured and solution-oriented manner and take pride in delivering excellent service

• Are willing to participate in a formalized 24/7 IT on-call schedule

As a person, you are curious and naturally take responsibility for seeing a task through to completion. You thrive in a work environment where priorities can change, and where one task may require deep technical focus, while the next involves helping a colleague move forward quickly and professionally.

We offer

• An exciting and varied position with a high degree of independence and responsibility

• The opportunity to work across a broad range of IT infrastructure and

modern cloud technologies

• A strong professional environment focused on development, collaboration, and knowledge sharing

• An attractive compensation package including a pension and health insurance, as well as a cafeteria plan and employee activities

• The job involves travel to our Danish and European locations

Process

Please upload your application and resume at https://bhj.com/career/vacant-jobs/ as soon as possible, as we review applications on an ongoing basis.

Please direct any questions about the position to Allan Kjærgaard, IT Services & Support Manager, alkj@bhj.dk, tel. 7435 1218.

jobs.occupation: Global Assoc Commercial Competitive Intelligence Director (1Year Contract)
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

In this one-year maternity cover, you will drive AI initiatives within Strategic Insights. You will find where AI can sharpen how we generate and share insights, including on the commercial competitive landscape in diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease, Working with the broader PSIA organisation on AI capabilities, you will help translate insights into clearer decisions at project, product and portfolio level.

What you’ll bring

You know AI well enough to see where it creates value, and your strength is turning that into use cases that get delivered and adopted. You don’t need to be a technical expert. You think independently, set the agenda yourself and communicate with clarity. We are open to candidates at different career stages, so the depth of experience we look for will vary with your background:

• An M.Sc. in Business, Medicine or Life/Pharmaceutical Sciences.

• Relevant experience in similar roles.

• Experience within the pharmaceutical or FMCG industry is highly preferred.

• Hands-on experience using AI tools in a business, insights or analytics setting, with a sound understanding of what AI can and cannot do.

• Experience developing and executing AI or digital use cases – from defining the business need to delivery and adoption.

• The ability to bridge business stakeholders and data or technical teams, translating needs into clear requirements and results into clear actions.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights.

• Strong communication skills, with the ability to present scientific, medical, commercial and AI-related topics clearly to diverse audiences, including senior management.

• An understanding of drug development, regulatory processes, commercial strategy and pharmaceutical value chains, with depth matching your seniority.

What you’ll do

Your focus is making AI work for insights: driving key use casesfrom ideation to delivery, and making sure the results reach the people who need them.

• Drive AI initiatives within Strategic Insights, identifying and prioritising use cases that improve how insights are generated, shared and used.

• Take use cases from idea to execution, working with data and technical colleagues to deliver tools and ways of working that teams adopt.

• Work with the broader PSIA organisation to build AI capabilities, share learnings and align on priorities.

• Translate insights, including on the commercial competitive landscape in diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease into clear recommendations for decisions at project, product and portfolio level.

• Communicate complex findings and AI outputs plainly to diverse audiences, including senior management.

• Encourage collaboration and knowledge sharing so successful AI practices spread across teams.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Commercial Competitive Intelligence team, which monitors, assesses and activates commercial competitive intelligence within core strategic areas in diabetes, obesity, Liver and Cardiovascular disease. The team is part of Strategic Insights, where you will work closely with colleagues in Customer & Consumer Insights and in Data, Analytics & AI Strategy.

Beyond Strategic Insights, you will partner with the broader PSIA organisation, as well as with Commercial teams and stakeholders across the value chain. Product & Portfolio Strategy drives commercial strategy, medical affairs and business development across all therapy areas, so the use cases you deliver can inform decisions well beyond your own team.

What you can expect here

You will step into a role with real influence. You will be trusted to set the agenda, make your voice heard and move AI initiatives from discussion to delivery. Novo is upskilling its entire workforce to advance AI as a main driver of innovation for people living with serious chronic diseases, and this role puts you at the centre of that work within Strategic Insights.

You will broaden your perspective by working across commercial, medical and data colleagues, and build new skills on the job. Because we are open to different career stages, your responsibilities and salary will be tailored to your experience.

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with a unique culture and strong results. We offer continuous learning, career development, and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Contract: 1-year maternity cover.Salary:  For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 847,000.00 to 1,245,100.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn AI use cases into better insights and sharper decisions, apply for the Global Assoc Competitive Intelligence Director role, a 1-year maternity cover, by 29 October 2026.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Medical Writer, Regulatory, Quality & Clinical Reporting, Søborg, Denmark
jobs.description:
This role is an exciting opportunity to blend scientific expertise with impactful communication, helping shape innovative healthcare solutions at a globally leading company like Novo Nordisk!

Your new the role

This is a permanent position in Medical Writing. In this role, your main responsibility will be to drive the preparation of complex clinical documents and act as a project manager. More specifically, you are expected to lead tasks such as:

• Plan, develop, and oversee high-quality regulatory and clinical documents in line with business needs and timelines.

• Prepare key documents such as study protocols, informed consent forms, investigator’s brochures, clinical summaries, and paediatric plans.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The product and the direction

Today we sell chat. Email is rolling out now, and phone and social follow. On top of that we are building the brain: a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers, understands why people buy, and why they do not, and acts on it while the buyer is still on the page. The effect is measured against a control group, so the shop can see what it means for revenue.

That moves the sale from a customer service tool to a conversation about growth, and revenue per customer can become several times what it is today.

Ownership of new business, partners and existing customers in one place. You run the process from first contact to signature, find out what works and write the sales process the rest of the company will follow.

Price, pitch, customer profile and process are yours. They change when they do not work, and the team is built as the numbers allow. Denmark is home turf, but we already have customers and partners in DACH and the Netherlands, and those markets grow from here.

About Userlink

Userlink runs AI agents in production at several hundred Nordic webshops, including Bahne, XL-BYG, Coolshop and Bygma. The agents handle the customer dialogue before and after the purchase, and every conversation ends up as structured data on demand and purchase barriers. The team is based in Odense.

The brain

The agents are the arms. The next layer is a system that brings together every signal about a webshop and its customers: conversations on chat, email, phone and social, on-site behaviour, orders, returns and reviews.

The system identifies the moments where a sale is won or lost and intervenes while the session is still live. It scores answer coverage per product and closes the gaps, quantifies objections and unmet demand, and traces returns back to the expectation that broke.

Learning happens across all webshops, more than six million visits a month, where patterns become visible that no single shop has the traffic to see. Every intervention is measured against a control group. The patterns are shared, the data stays with each shop.

The hard problems are retrieval and evaluation of LLM output at scale, data isolation when patterns are shared across customers, latency in real-time flows, and attribution that holds up under scrutiny.

The stack

Java with Spring Boot, React and MongoDB, with language models and vector search on top. Moving the backend to C# and .NET is under consideration.

The role

Technical ownership of the platform: architecture, code quality, operations, security and prioritisation, combined with hands-on development every day. Standards for review, testing, monitoring and releases, and recruiting the next developers.

Decisions are made on arguments, not titles. Ideas get challenged regardless of where they come from, and the best one wins.

jobs.occupation: PhD in In-Operando Diagnostics of Li-ion and Post-Li-ion Batteries Using Acoustic Technology
jobs.description:
At AAU Energy, a PhD stipend position is available within the general study program. The stipend is open for appointment from 15 November 2026 or soon hereafter. The duration of the position is three years.

Your work tasks
Battery performance assessment and diagnostics rely today on standardised electrical measurements complemented by post-mortem analysis. None of these methods is suited for in-operando diagnostics, as they are either destructive or require the battery to be taken out of its daily operation. Acoustic techniques, based either on passive listening to acoustic emissions or on active ultrasound signal injection, have recently been proposed as an alternative; however, further research is needed to establish the relationship between materials degradation and the sensed acoustic signals. The aim of this PhD project is to establish a mechanistic understanding of the coupling between battery ageing mechanisms and measured acoustic signals, and to translate this understanding into a diagnostic method applicable to both Li-ion and post-Li-ion chemistries.

You will start by reviewing the state of the art in acoustic-based battery diagnostics, and you will then design and build a set-up for sensing acoustic emissions in coin cells. Using this set-up, you will carry out degradation tests over a wide range of operating conditions with simultaneous acoustic and electrical measurements, and you will analyse how the acoustic signatures relate to the electrical ones and to the underlying degradation mechanisms. On this basis, you will develop an acoustic-based, physics-validated model for battery diagnostics; the resulting algorithm is targeted to be at least 25% more accurate than conventional impedance-based estimation and at least 50% less energy demanding than traditional diagnostic approaches. While most of the experimental work will be carried out at coin-cell level, a proof of concept at single-layer pouch-cell level is expected, which will facilitate further demonstration towards innovation.

The work will be supported by critical analysis of the results, benchmarking against the state of the art, and high-quality publications and conference presentations. In addition to the research activities, you will contribute to teaching and to the supervision of student projects, as well as to broader dissemination activities within the department.

The position is offered in relation to the research group Batteries, and the PhD Student will be positioned to the section for Power Electronics Systems Integration and Materials.

Your competencies 
We are looking for a motivated PhD candidate who is eager to work at the intersection of battery testing, sensing instrumentation and signal processing, and who enjoys combining fundamental understanding with hands-on experimental work. The ideal candidate is curious and persistent in the laboratory, excels at troubleshooting, can plan and execute experiments independently, and motivated to collaborate closely with colleagues in an international and interdisciplinary environment.

Applicants must hold an M.Sc. degree in electrical engineering, energy engineering or mechatronics. Experience with one or more of the following will be considered an advantage: electrical characterisation of batteries, acoustic or ultrasonic sensing and laboratory instrumentation, and signal processing and data-driven modelling (e.g., in MATLAB or Python). Experience with Problem Based Learning (PBL) is required, as the PhD student will be involved in the supervision of BSc and MSc student projects. Strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken, are required, as the project will be carried out in an international research environment. Danish language skills are highly desirable and will support co-supervision of BSc student projects; however, they are not a formal requirement.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are    
AAU Energy is a research department at Aalborg University dedicated to the development of clean and sustainable energy systems. Our activities cover electrical, thermal and mechatronic energy technologies, and we work closely with industrial partners, utilities and other academic environments to address real world energy challenges.

Aalborg University has been ranked as the best university in Europe within energy research and is among the very best universities worldwide in this field. At AAU Energy you will be part of a top international environment where research, innovation and collaboration are used to develop solutions to global challenges such as the green transition and future energy systems.

The department is located in both Aalborg and Esbjerg, and this position is based at the Aalborg campus. AAU Energy employs around 250 staff members at different career stages and with diverse national and disciplinary backgrounds, which creates an international and interdisciplinary research environment with many opportunities for collaboration and knowledge sharing. English is widely used as working language in both research and teaching, which supports the integration of international colleagues.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk.

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
• Curriculum Vitae (CV)
• Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
• Other relevant documents
The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world
Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.
